assessment_summary: The statement is false because there exist trees on n vertices (2 <= n <= 7) where the diameter is not twice the radius. For instance, the path graph on 2 vertices (P2) has a diameter of 1 and a radius of 1, so diam(P2) != 2 * rad(P2). Another counterexample is the path graph on 4 vertices (P4) with diameter 3 and radius 2. Since the mathematical claim itself is demonstrably false, no valid proof can be constructed.
counterexample: Path graph on 2 vertices (P2). diam(P2) = 1, rad(P2) = 1, so diam(P2) != 2 * rad(P2).
